profile_text.body:
The Allen Institute for AI (also known as Ai2) is a nonprofit AI research organization founded in 2014 by Paul Allen and headquartered in Seattle, WA. The institute is led by Ali Farhadi and describes itself as conducting high-impact research and engineering to tackle key problems in artificial intelligence. Its stated research principles emphasize openness, collaboration, and inclusivity, with a focus on producing safe, ethical, and trustworthy AI systems. The organization maintains partnerships with the University of Washington's Paul G. Allen School of Computer Science and Engineering, the NSF on an open multimodal AI infrastructure project, and Google Cloud for development of open AI models and platforms.

Ai2's work spans both foundational AI research and applied domains including climate science, agriculture, wildfire management, and wildlife protection. Among its tracked products are OLMo, an open-source language model developed with fully open training data and an emphasis on research transparency, and Semantic Scholar, an AI-powered academic search tool offering paper summaries and citation graphs. Both products reflect the institute's nonprofit, research-oriented mission.

The held facts confirm Ai2 is a registered presence on the site, classified as a research lab and verified in August 2026, with no litigation or MCP server entries on record.
